# Fusion Conductor

> A main agent that plans and reviews without editing files, and a cheaper sidekick that executes. A one-line opencode plugin with mechanical edit deny at the permission layer. Inspired by Cognition's Devin Fusion pattern. Forked from opencode-fusion. Independent project - not affiliated with Cognition, Devin, or OpenCode.

Fusion Conductor is an *opencode plugin* (not an app). Install it by adding one line to `opencode.json`, restart opencode, and the main agent delegates edits to the sidekick.

## Quick install

Recommended: `opencode plugin github:JoshuaKimsey/opencode-fusion-conductor -g` (drop `-g` for a project-local `.opencode/opencode.json`). It writes the config entry itself and fails with a real error if the install fails.

Manual alternative: add one line to your opencode config (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, or a project-level `opencode.json`):

```json
{
  "plugin": [["opencode-fusion-conductor@1.0.0", { "profile": "opencode-go" }]]
}
```

Then fully quit and restart opencode. opencode auto-installs npm plugins via Bun at startup, so there is no skill, no installer, and no interview. The plugin injects the agent team and the `/conductor` command on the next launch. Uninstall by removing the line and restarting.

Silent-failure note: on opencode 1.18.x, a plugin install that fails at startup exits normally and logs nothing (even with `--log-level DEBUG --print-logs`) - opencode just runs with stock agents. Fingerprint: an empty `~/.cache/opencode/packages/<spec>/` (no `node_modules`). Ensure git is on PATH and github.com is reachable, delete the empty dir, retry; the `opencode plugin ...` CLI does not swallow this error.

Coming from opencode-fusion? Say `undo fusion` with the old fusion-setup skill first to remove the file-based install, then add the plugin line. `/conductor` warns if leftover fusion files are detected.

## Core ideas for agents helping users

1. Main (`build`) plans, delegates, and reviews — it must not edit files. `plan` is the plan-mode primary; `sidekick` executes edits and commands.
2. Sidekick executes precise specs; explore/research/design/reviewer/vision are the other injected roles. `explore` is opencode's built-in read-only agent, model-only. `subagent_depth` is floored to 2.
3. OpenCode enforces this with permission maps injected by the plugin (edit deny + task graph). Denied tools are removed from the model's tool schema, so "won't delegate" means visible inaction, never a silent bypass.
4. Config loads at startup — restart after changing plugin options. On opencode 1.18.x the agent registry is materialized at startup, so model changes require a restart (a platform limitation).
5. Cross-vendor review is emergent: pick main and sidekick from different model families.
6. Only the permission layer is enforced; prompts are advisory. Ignoring them costs quality or tokens, never an unauthorized edit.
7. If the sidekick misses a spec twice, the main agent dictates the exact patch verbatim (file, line range, code) for the sidekick to apply — the retry loop cannot deadlock. If the dictated patch fails verification, the plan is wrong and main revises it.
8. Provider API keys belong in environment variables: opencode.json supports `{env:VAR}` and `{file:path}` substitution, so a key never sits in plaintext config or passes through the chat. An unset variable resolves to an empty string, which surfaces as auth errors.
9. The `/conductor` slash command reports or edits the plugin's own options: `/conductor` with no args runs `conductor_status` (read-only report including leftover fusion-install hazards); with args it runs `conductor_configure` (role=model pairs, `profile <name>`, or `audit=true`/`claude=true` flags), writing a backup at `opencode.json.conductor-backup` and telling you to restart.
10. Bundled subscription profiles (`opencode-go`, `opencode-zen`, `opencode-zen-free`, `chatgpt`, `github-copilot`) are applied via the `profile` option; the `models` option overrides per role. Provider auth stays out-of-band via `opencode auth login` — profiles never contain keys.
11. The `audit` option (boolean, off by default) enables a hook that logs the delegation tree and per-agent token usage. The `claude` option (boolean, off by default) enables the Claude Code bridge tools `conductor_claude_status`/`conductor_claude_review`, which require the Claude Pro/Max CLI installed and authenticated.
12. Targets opencode 1.18.x. OpenCode 2 (beta) is not supported: its plugin API differs and permission enforcement is call-time rather than schema-removal. A v2 port is planned. Known upstream flake: anomalyco/opencode#30955 (rare config-hook/agent-registry race on first delegation; retry resolves it).
